title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling & Benchmarking Playbook
author: Alex Chen
summary: Canonical reference for serving-runtime architecture, kernel scheduling heuristics, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite usage, recent release notes, known issues, and operational runbooks. For runtime engineers, SREs, and release engineers.
components: runtime-orchestrator: request routing and placement; serving-runtime-worker: GPU process that loads weights, manages KV cache, executes kernels; kernel-scheduler: in-worker kernel selection and CUDA stream scheduling; cache-service: global prefix/KV cache; perf-agent: trace/metric collector.
request_flow: 1) API -> runtime-orchestrator selects pool by policy (hosted/dedicated/private). 2) Request forwarded to serving-runtime-worker; worker consults cache-service for prefix hits. 3) kernel-scheduler chooses kernels based on model variant, seq_len, dtype, and hardware. 4) GPU execution with continuous batching; KV cache updated; response streamed.
slos_and_thresholds: API SLO examples: p50 token latency < 50ms; p95 short-request end-to-end < 150ms; p99 end-to-end < 500ms; Availability 99.95% monthly. Alerts: serving-latency-p95-high (p95 > 200ms for 10m -> PagerDuty); serving-queue-depth-high (worker queue > 800 for 5m -> Page); gpu-memory-pressure (GPU mem > 92% -> Page).
kernel_scheduling_design: Goals: minimize tail latency, maximize utilization, keep deterministic behavior. Inputs: model architecture (attention type, layer layout), dtype/quantization, sequence length distribution, hardware capabilities. Heuristics: prefer fused kernels for short sequences to cut launch overhead; use blocked/long-seq attention kernels when seq_len > 1024; for quantized models prefer int8 kernels when accuracy passes eval; fall back to FP16 when regressions detected. Runtime policy supports per-worker overrides and dynamic metrics-driven adjustments.
profiling_playbook: Purpose: repeatable process for actionable CPU/GPU traces. Steps: 1) Capture representative workload using perf-harness replay. 2) Lightweight tracing: aggregate metrics (token/sec, batch size distribution, queue length). Example: ./perf-agent collect --duration 300 --out /tmp/runtime_metrics.json. 3) GPU tracing: nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=/tmp/nsys_trace ${SERVING_BINARY} --config run-config.yaml. 4) Kernel-level: ncu --target-processes all --metrics gld_throughput,gst_throughput,warp_executionEfficiency -o /tmp/ncu_report ./serving-runtime-worker --worker-id wf-23. 5) CPU sampling: perf or py-spy for scheduler/RPC stacks. 6) Post-process: upload traces to s3://perf-trace-bucket and create a triage issue with reproduction steps, observed vs expected metrics, suspected root cause, mitigations.
benchmarking_suite: Repo: internal perf-harness (bench-runner). Typical run: ./bench-runner --model gptj-6b --variant q4_0 --seq 512 --batch 8 --duration 600 --out metrics/gptj_q4_512_b8.json. Important flags: --replay-trace <trace.json>, --steady-warmup <seconds>, --enable-caching true|false. Bench metrics emitted as JSON: tokens_per_second, p50/p95/p99 latency (token and end-to-end), average_gpu_utilization, kernel-level breakdown. Interpretation guidance: if queueing >> kernel time, increase worker count or reduce batch_max_size; for large seq jobs verify blocked-attention kernels engaged; check kernel fallback rates in kernel-selection heatmap.
release_notes_summary: v1.12.0 (2026-01-20): dynamic kernel-selection policy added (p99 ~ -18% on medium-length workloads); KV cache hit latency improved by ~12ms; fixed race in batch aggregator causing dropped tokens under ~1000 RPS. v1.11.3 (2025-11-30): fixed memory leak in quantized weight loader (q4_0/q5_1); improved kernel timing telemetry.
known_issues: ISSUE-RT-142: intermittent p99 spikes for seq_len 2048 on A100s. Symptoms: p99 > 1.2s. Workaround: set KERNEL_POLICY=blocked_attention_priority or pin to model-variant-longseq. Owner: Marcus Rivera. ISSUE-RT-157: fallback to generic kernel on mixed-dtype layers. Symptoms: throughput drop ~30%. Workaround: convert model to unified dtype or use hosted-compat fallback policy. Owner: Priya Kapoor.
runtime_runbooks: Incident: sustained high p95 latency. Steps: 1) Verify alert and Grafana dashboard 'Serving Runtime - Latency'. 2) Quick checks: kubectl get pods -n serving | grep CrashLoopBackOff; ./admin-cli worker-metrics --time 10m --format table. 3) Root cause categories: queueing, GPU saturation, kernel fallback. 4) Mitigations: scale up worker pool +30% (./orchestrator scale --pool serving-prod --delta 30%), enable burst nodes, enable routing fallback to smaller model variant, set KERNEL_POLICY=fast-path on affected workers and restart. 5) Post-incident: run bench-runner against production replay for 30m and attach traces. Incident: OOM on worker. Steps: identify worker with GPU mem >99%, mark draining, restart worker process, inspect /var/log/serving/mem-alloc.log, if recurrent reduce batch_max_size or deploy larger GPU node type.
team_wiki_onboarding: Quickstart for new runtime engineers: read this doc; run local bench-runner with a tiny model and reproduce a simple request; complete profiling playbook with nsys and upload artifact; shadow on-call for 2 weeks. Helpful dashboards: Serving Runtime - Latency (Grafana), Kernel Selection Heatmap, GPU Fleet Utilization. On-call pager: serving-runtime-sre (PD ID: PDRT-43).
appendix_common_commands: Dump worker metrics (JSON): ./admin-cli worker-metrics --worker wf-23 --output json > /tmp/wf23.json. Quick trace upload: aws s3 cp /tmp/nsys_trace.qd s3://perf-trace-bucket/$(date +%F)-nsys_trace.qd. Toggle kernel policy: kubectl exec -n serving wf-23 -- /bin/sh -c "export KERNEL_POLICY=fast-path && svcctl reload-config".
